implementation: Hash-pinned extension of existing scoped job connection; only own Service.GetProcesses, no args, typed a(sus), no new mutation/global API, native symbol or loader.
Up to 32 unique process IDs and 65536 decoded text bytes; private command lines are never included in public quiescence results.
Two recursive process observations plus current/known job checks, exact invocation and final unit/profile/group checks.

Empty process lists alone are insufficient: two group observations also require strictly zero TasksCurrent or explicit manager deassignment after a fixed active cgroup was observed in the same invocation.
UINT64_MAX task count is unknown, not zero; missing/errored/changed facts fail or remain pending; no ENOENT or ENODEV success inference.
A same-invocation release is a manager release observation, not proof that the former path currently exists and is empty.
Staged worker session now derives empty from typed recursive/process/task/release facts rather than a direct cgroup-empty callback; ownership provenance remains explicitly simulated.
testEvidenceNotes: Initial new module run failed on missing implementation; not a behavioral red-test proof.

Cases cover residual descendants, main/control processes outside the cgroup, nonzero/unknown tasks, group release during reads, invocation changes, actual automatic drift sealing, malformed and oversized replies, late enumeration, empty reply cleanup failure, pending jobs and permission/unsupported-method errors.

All 43 prior job/manager assertions and 2 prior combined session cases are retained against the extension. Final selected batch is 65 schema/compatibility, 5 session, 25 staged, 29 kernel-reader and 142 existing-session cases; no rerun counts accumulated.
Negative sessions preserve artifacts and failed cleanup at exhausted simulated budget; no deadline extension or uncertain close retry.
The combined fixture binds a verified test-source import through an exact AST import replacement, not arbitrary source mutation.
Command limits are decoded-data bounds, not a bound on native bus-library reply allocation before decoding. Native memory/outer watchdog checks remain required.
limitations: Only in-memory C ABI/kernel/FIFO replies and simulated timing were used. Windows wall time and simulated deadlines do not prove VPS CPU/memory/runtime limits.

Manager/library/root/socket provenance, full prepared-unit security profile and installed GetProcesses/TasksCurrent/release semantics still need trusted assembly and separately scoped native validation.
Cross-property samples are not atomic and do not prevent a future authorized start.
Public cgroup/job facts are separate from artifact ownership; no native ownership proof is asserted.
These are selected related suites, not a full product regression or production acceptance.
Historical AddRef contract failure remains separately recorded, not rerun or resolved.
synchronization: Sanitized verification only; no private experimental source, process commands, raw errors or credentials.
